rationale: The candidate reads as a compact, faceted, near-hexagonal block with some silhouette articulation, but the four views show no meaningful public void, undercut, court, or active threshold responding to the verified access edge. The mass is coherent as a single object, yet it remains semantically sealed and more like a generic sculpted block than a neighborhood-living building with an active street ground, one clear public void/terrace, and calm upper massing. The top view especially suggests a simple enclosed footprint with no carved access logic, while the elevation views do not establish a legible entry seam. It is not visibly colliding or fragmented, so repair integrity is decent, but program fit fails because the visible mass does not support the required public-ground relation.
